meta.title: The Weekly Stampede
meta.subtitle: Week of 21–25 Sep 2026 · gold miners, India, emerging markets and equities
meta.sourceLine: Closes: FT, AP, NSE, US Treasury, ICE

questions.ask: Is one hike the end of it — or the start of a cycle, with the ten-year at 5.1%?
facts: 16 of the Fed's 18 officials expect at least one more hike this year, and four expect two (Fed projections, 16 Sep).
Markets price roughly a 70% chance of a hike in October (CME FedWatch, 23 Sep).
New York Fed's Williams (24 Sep): another hike this year is “reasonable”, but he would not commit to October.
The next inflation read the Fed targets, August PCE, is out on Wednesday 30 September (BEA).

questions.ask: The miners move about twice as far as gold, both ways. Does that still make sense 22% below the record?
facts: This week GDX rose 3.6% and fell 4.4% on consecutive days, while gold moved −0.2% and −1.3%.
Gold is about 22% below its January record of $5,595 (Reuters, 22 Sep).
Kinross now plans on $4,350 gold, with all-in sustaining costs of about $1,850–1,900 an ounce, after cutting output guidance (23 Sep).
Goldman Sachs kept its $4,900 end-2026 gold target (Kitco, 23 Sep).

questions.ask: India after the insurance shock and six straight weekly falls: value, or wait for the RBI on 7 October?
facts: Foreign investors have sold ₹2.45 lakh crore of Indian equities in 2026, more than in all of 2025 (Angel One, 20 Sep).
Monday to Wednesday, domestic funds bought ₹9,259 crore while foreign investors sold ₹2,769 crore (NSE provisional).
The Nifty fell for six straight weeks to 18 September, its longest run since 2020 (HDFC Sky).
The RBI decides on 7 October; the IRDAI consultation on distribution costs is open until 25 October.

sourcing: Closing levels checked against FT Markets Data where FT publishes them: S&P 500, Brent, Nifty 50, Nasdaq, FTSE 100, GDX, EEM and the Hang Seng.

Otherwise two independent sources that agree: AP (US indices), US Treasury (yields), ICE via Reuters (Brent), NSE via Kotak Neo and Liquide (India), Yahoo Finance and Investing.com (COMEX December gold, GDX, GDXJ).
Taiwan, Korea and the CSI 300 come from Focus Taiwan, Seoul Economic Daily and Investing.com/Xinhua; FT's free pages don't carry them.
Fed decision and projections: federalreserve.gov. PMIs: S&P Global and HSBC flash releases. PB Fintech: BusinessToday, Ventura Securities.
Figures run to Thursday's close for India and Asia and Wednesday's close for the US, gold and oil. Update the Friday slide and the scoreboard before presenting.

days.label: Weekend
days.moodNote: A 25bp hike with 16 of 18 officials pencilling in more — higher for longer is the starting point.
days.headline: The Fed hiked for the first time in about three years — and sixteen of its eighteen officials want to go again.

chart.title: Where the Fed sees rates at the end of 2026
chart.note: Number of FOMC participants · Federal Reserve projections, 16 Sep

notes: Right — this week comes down to one question: is the Fed done?

Last Wednesday it raised rates for the first time in about three years — a quarter point, to three and three-quarters to four per cent. The chart is what matters: sixteen of the eighteen officials expect at least one more hike this year, and four expect two.
So we started the week with the ten-year at five per cent and Brent above a hundred dollars. That's the backdrop for everything that follows.

days.label: Monday
days.moodNote: Nasdaq +2.3% to a record on AI and chips, with Brent down 3.4% as the Hormuz premium faded.
days.headline: An AI-led rally took the Nasdaq to a record close, helped by Brent falling back to $100.

chart.title: Stocks up, oil down — until Wednesday
chart.note: Rebased, Fri 18 Sep close = 0 · AP, ICE; S&P and Brent confirmed on FT

notes: Monday was the good day. The S&P was up one and a half per cent, and the Nasdaq more than two, to a record close.

That was an AI and chip rally — AMD up about ten per cent and through a trillion dollars in value, Meta up around eleven. Oil helped: Brent fell three and a half per cent as the Hormuz risk premium came out.
Watch the oil line — on Wednesday it turns back up, and the rally goes with it.

days.label: Tuesday
days.moodNote: GDX +3.6% and the juniors +4.3% on a day gold itself slipped 0.2%.
days.headline: Gold barely moved and the miners jumped 3.6% — that is what a beta of two looks like, and it works both ways.

chart.title: The miners' beta, both ways
chart.note: Rebased, Fri 18 Sep close = 0 · COMEX Dec gold, GDX, GDXJ closes; GDX confirmed on FT

notes: If you own gold miners, Tuesday is the one to remember. Gold barely moved — down a fifth of a per cent. But GDX, the big miners ETF, was up three point six per cent, and the juniors more than four.
Then look at Wednesday on the chart: the same stocks gave it all back and more. That's the miners' beta — roughly twice the move in gold — working both ways.
And gold is still about twenty-two per cent below its January record, just under five thousand six hundred dollars.

days.label: Wednesday
days.moodNote: PMI 58.4 against 56.0 expected; the 10-year up 15bp to 5.11%; GDX down 4.4%.
days.headline: A red-hot US PMI sent the 10-year to 5.11%, its highest since 2007, and put an October hike firmly in play.

stats.label: Gold miners (GDX)
stats.note: Kinross cuts output guidance after the close

charts.title: Flash composite PMI, September — points above 50
charts.note: S&P Global / HSBC flash, 22–24 Sep · 50 = no change on the month

notes: Wednesday changed the week. The US flash PMI came in at fifty-eight point four against fifty-six expected — the strongest in five years, with input costs rising at the fastest pace since 2022.

The market read that as more hikes. The ten-year jumped fifteen basis points to five point one one per cent, its highest since 2007, and pricing moved to about a seventy per cent chance of an October hike.
Gold fell, the miners dropped more than four per cent, and Kinross cut its guidance after the close. And note India on the left — the strongest PMI outside the US.

days.label: Thursday
days.moodNote: Nifty −1.64% to a three-month low, with India VIX up 23% and the rupee at 95.96.
days.headline: India gave back the week in a day: oil, US yields and a regulatory shock to insurers all landed at once.

charts.title: Nifty 50, daily close
charts.note: NSE · Thursday close confirmed on FT

charts.title: Who's buying India? Net flows, Mon–Wed

notes: Thursday was India's turn. The Nifty fell one point six per cent to a three-month low, and the Sensex lost more than twelve hundred points.

Two things hit at once. Brent back above a hundred and five dollars and US yields near a twenty-year high are a bad mix for an oil importer. And the insurance regulator published a draft capping distribution costs — PB Fintech, which owns Policybazaar, closed down thirty-six per cent.

The right-hand chart shows who's holding this market up: foreign investors sold nearly twenty-eight hundred crore from Monday to Wednesday, and domestic funds bought over nine thousand. The RBI meets on the seventh of October, and the market's now pricing a possible hike.

days.label: Friday
days.moodNote: Emerging markets outside China are up on the week on chips. What decides Friday is whether the US 10-year holds above 5% into the weekend.
days.headline: Chips carried emerging markets — Taiwan at a record, Korea's exports booming — while China slipped on a short truce.

stats.label: CSI 300
stats.note: Thursday · truce extended only two months

chart.title: Emerging-market equities, Fri 18 Sep to latest close
chart.note: KOSPI and MSCI EM to Wed (Korea shut Thu for Chuseok); others to Thu

notes: Across emerging markets, the week was about chips. Taiwan closed at a record on Wednesday, and Korea was up nearly three per cent before it shut for Chuseok — its chip exports so far this month are up more than two and a half times on a year ago.
China was the weak spot: the trade truce was extended by only two months, and the CSI 300 fell one point seven per cent on Thursday.
Today's US data is second-tier. The inflation number the Fed targets, PCE, isn't out until next Wednesday.

days.label: The Close
days.pendingLabel: Asia to Thursday · US to Wednesday
days.moodNote: Rates won the week: the miners, gold and India all fell; only the chip trade held up.
days.headline: Higher for longer won the week. The AI trade held up, but gold, the miners and India all paid for a 5% ten-year.
days.verdictNote: These run to the latest close — Asia on Thursday, the US and gold on Wednesday. The scoreboard settles on Friday's close, and your call settles with it.
notes: So here's the scoreboard, from last Friday to the latest close. The theme is higher for longer.
The miners are down two per cent, gold two and a half, India just over one. The strength was in the chip-heavy markets and the Nasdaq.
Friday's closes go in once we have them — but on our three themes, rates won this week. It's the bear.
